OpenPipelines takes single-cell and spatial data from raw sequencing output, or from imaging-based spatial platforms, to a processed, standardized dataset.
This includes ingestion, per-sample processing (filtering, quality control, normalization), integration, and downstream analysis.
The workflows and tools used depend on the data modality and the technology platform.

::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple" title="New to OpenPipelines?"}
This page maps all OpenPipelines workflows end to end. If terms like *component*, *workflow*, or *Viash Hub* are unfamiliar, start with reading the core [Concepts](../concepts/index.qmd) instead.
:::

## Demultiplexing (optional) {#demultiplexing}

If your sequencing provider delivers raw Illumina BCL files, convert them to per-sample FASTQ files.
This step is **often already performed upstream** by your sequencing provider, but is also available within OpenPipelines.
It only applies to sequencing-based data (single-cell, or the sequencing-based Visium spatial platform).

The `ingestion/demux` workflow supports three demultiplexers selected via
`--demultiplexer`:

- **bcl2fastq**: legacy Illumina tool
- **BCL Convert**: current Illumina general-purpose demultiplexer
- **cellranger mkfastq** (deprecated): 10x Genomics wrapper with
  convenience features for 10x libraries

If you already have FASTQ files or a pre-built count matrix, skip directly to
[Ingestion](#ingestion).

| Workflow | Package | Description |
|---|---|---|
| [`ingestion/demux`](../reference/openpipeline/v4.2.0/workflows/ingestion/demux.qmd) | [<span class="swatch openpipeline"></span>`openpipeline`]{.pkg-tag .pkg-openpipeline} | BCL → FASTQ demultiplexing (bcl2fastq, BCL Convert, mkfastq (deprecated)) |

## Ingestion {#ingestion}

Ingestion workflows convert raw platform outputs to a standardized MuData (`.h5mu`) format.
For single-cell and sequencing-based spatial data (Visium, Visium HD), this involves aligning sequencing reads to a reference genome, assigning them to cells/spatial coordinates, and counting them by UMI.
Imaging-based spatial platforms (Xenium, CosMx, AVITI24) skip high-throughput library prep and alignment; instead, the vendor's primary output files (matrices, feature locations, and cell segmentation boundaries) are converted to standardized structures.

::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple" title="Guides"}
[Ingest data](../guides/ingest-10x.qmd) and [Ingest spatial data](../guides/ingest-spatial.qmd) cover workflow selection, reference genome setup, and examples.
:::

::: {.panel-tabset}

### Single-cell

OpenPipelines supports 10x Genomics and BD Rhapsody. Which mapper to use depends on the platform and library type (gene expression only, or gene expression + ADT/HTO + VDJ).

### Spatial

Sequencing-based Visium data is mapped from FASTQs with Space Ranger, the same way single-cell data is.
Imaging-based platforms (Xenium, CosMx, AVITI24) are converted directly from the vendor's own output, since they do not generate FASTQ files or require read mapping.

| Workflow / component | Package | Description |
|---|---|---|
| [`ingestion/spaceranger_mapping`](../reference/openpipeline_spatial/v0.7.0/workflows/ingestion/spaceranger_mapping.qmd) | [<span class="swatch openpipeline_spatial"></span>`openpipeline_spatial`]{.pkg-tag .pkg-openpipeline_spatial} | Space Ranger mapping for Visium (sequencing-based) |

| [`convert/from_xenium_to_h5mu`](../reference/openpipeline_spatial/v0.7.0/convert/from_xenium_to_h5mu.qmd) | [<span class="swatch openpipeline_spatial"></span>`openpipeline_spatial`]{.pkg-tag .pkg-openpipeline_spatial} | 10x Xenium output → H5MU (imaging-based) |
| [`convert/from_cosmx_to_h5mu`](../reference/openpipeline_spatial/v0.7.0/convert/from_cosmx_to_h5mu.qmd) | [<span class="swatch openpipeline_spatial"></span>`openpipeline_spatial`]{.pkg-tag .pkg-openpipeline_spatial} | CosMx output → H5MU (imaging-based) |
| [`convert/from_cells2stats_to_h5mu`](../reference/openpipeline_spatial/v0.7.0/convert/from_cells2stats_to_h5mu.qmd) | [<span class="swatch openpipeline_spatial"></span>`openpipeline_spatial`]{.pkg-tag .pkg-openpipeline_spatial} | AVITI24 (cells2stats) output → H5MU |

## QC report (optional) {#qc-report}

Raw ingested data holds more than real cells or spots: empty droplets that only captured ambient RNA, dying or damaged cells with a high mitochondrial fraction, and doublets where two cells were captured together.
A QC report profiles these signals across your dataset so you can choose sensible, data-driven filtering thresholds before processing.

::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple" title="Guides"}
[Generate a QC report](../guides/qc-report.qmd) and [Generate a spatial QC report](../guides/qc-report-spatial.qmd) cover reading the report and choosing thresholds.
:::

::: {.panel-tabset}

## Process samples {#process-samples}

These workflows filter out the empty droplets, damaged cells and doublets described above, then continue with the rest of per-sample processing: concatenation across samples, normalization, highly variable feature selection, and PCA.
The result is one processed, normalized cohort object ready for integration.

::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple" title="Guides"}
[Process samples](../guides/process-samples.qmd) and [Process spatial samples](../guides/process-spatial.qmd) cover filtering strategies, the processing sequence, and threshold choices in detail.
:::

::: {.panel-tabset}

### Single-cell

| Workflow / component | Package | Description |
|---|---|---|
| [`multiomics/process_samples`](../reference/openpipeline/v4.2.0/workflows/multiomics/process_samples.qmd) | [<span class="swatch openpipeline"></span>`openpipeline`]{.pkg-tag .pkg-openpipeline} | End-to-end processing for single-cell data |
| [`correction/cellbender_remove_background`](../reference/openpipeline/v4.2.0/correction/cellbender_remove_background.qmd) | [<span class="swatch openpipeline"></span>`openpipeline`]{.pkg-tag .pkg-openpipeline} | Optional standalone step: remove ambient RNA from raw counts |

::: {.callout-note}
`process_samples` processes RNA, protein (ADT), and GDO.
Other modalities, such as ATAC and VDJ, are kept in the output unchanged.
For ATAC QC, use the standalone `calculate_atac_qc_metrics` component.
:::

## Integration {#integration}

Samples from different donors, sequencing runs, or library preparations often include batch effects that complicate analysis.
Integration workflows remove these effects, producing a clean multi-sample dataset for analysis.
OpenPipelines supports several integration methods operating on different data representations, each with different assumptions and strengths.

::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple" title="Guides"}
[Integrate across samples](../guides/integrate.qmd) covers method selection in detail.
:::

| Workflow | Package | Method | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| [`integration/harmony_leiden`](../reference/openpipeline/v4.2.0/workflows/integration/harmony_leiden.qmd) | [<span class="swatch openpipeline"></span>`openpipeline`]{.pkg-tag .pkg-openpipeline} | Harmony | Iterative linear correction of the PCA embedding |
| [`integration/scvi_leiden`](../reference/openpipeline/v4.2.0/workflows/integration/scvi_leiden.qmd) | [<span class="swatch openpipeline"></span>`openpipeline`]{.pkg-tag .pkg-openpipeline} | scVI | Variational autoencoder that learns an integrated latent space |
| [`integration/scanorama_leiden`](../reference/openpipeline/v4.2.0/workflows/integration/scanorama_leiden.qmd) | [<span class="swatch openpipeline"></span>`openpipeline`]{.pkg-tag .pkg-openpipeline} | Scanorama | Mutual-nearest-neighbor integration (panorama stitching) |
| [`integration/bbknn_leiden`](../reference/openpipeline/v4.2.0/workflows/integration/bbknn_leiden.qmd) | [<span class="swatch openpipeline"></span>`openpipeline`]{.pkg-tag .pkg-openpipeline} | BBKNN | Batch-balanced neighbor graph; produces no corrected embedding |
| [`integration/totalvi_leiden`](../reference/openpipeline/v4.2.0/workflows/integration/totalvi_leiden.qmd) | [<span class="swatch openpipeline"></span>`openpipeline`]{.pkg-tag .pkg-openpipeline} | totalVI | Joint RNA + protein (CITE-seq) model; corrects both modalities |
| [`single_cell/parallel_integration`](../reference/openpipeline_composed/v0.3.0/single_cell/parallel_integration.qmd) | [<span class="swatch openpipeline_composed"></span>`openpipeline_composed`]{.pkg-tag .pkg-openpipeline_composed} | multiple | Runs several of the above methods on the same input and merges their outputs |

## Downstream {#downstream}

These workflows move beyond standard processing to perform biological analysis.

### Annotation {#annotation}

A key downstream task is annotation: assigning labels to clusters or individual observations.
In OpenPipelines, this is always reference-based, transferring labels from an in-house model, an open-source model, or a reference dataset.
Which tool to use depends on the available references, the tissue, and the biological question.

::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple" title="Guides"}
[Annotate cell types](../guides/annotate.qmd) covers method selection for single-cell data.
:::

| Workflow | Package | Description |
|---|---|---|
| [`annotation/harmony_knn`](../reference/openpipeline/v4.2.0/workflows/annotation/harmony_knn.qmd) | [<span class="swatch openpipeline"></span>`openpipeline`]{.pkg-tag .pkg-openpipeline} | KNN label transfer from a reference atlas |
| [`annotation/scvi_knn`](../reference/openpipeline/v4.2.0/workflows/annotation/scvi_knn.qmd) | [<span class="swatch openpipeline"></span>`openpipeline`]{.pkg-tag .pkg-openpipeline} | KNN label transfer using scVI latent space |
| [`annotation/scanvi_scarches`](../reference/openpipeline/v4.2.0/workflows/annotation/scanvi_scarches.qmd) | [<span class="swatch openpipeline"></span>`openpipeline`]{.pkg-tag .pkg-openpipeline} | scANVI/scArches label transfer |
| [`annotation/celltypist`](../reference/openpipeline/v4.2.0/workflows/annotation/celltypist.qmd) | [<span class="swatch openpipeline"></span>`openpipeline`]{.pkg-tag .pkg-openpipeline} | CellTypist marker-based annotation |
